title: Psalms of Solomon — Hobah Translation
about: A collection of eighteen Jewish psalms from the late Second Temple period, commonly connected with the upheavals surrounding Pompey's capture of Jerusalem. The collection is especially important for its language about righteousness, divine judgment, Jerusalem, and the expected Davidic Messiah.

translation.status: Hobah complete modern-English rendering from public-domain historical translation
translation.base_text: The complete eighteen-psalm public-domain witness in Rutherford H. Platt Jr., The Forgotten Books of Eden (1926), chapter pages hosted by the Internet Sacred Text Archive mirror, representing the Greek tradition through earlier public-domain scholarly translation
translation.method: Complete conservative Hobah modernization of the public-domain historical English witness. Psalm order and content are retained while archaic English is normalized. This is original Hobah modern-English wording based on a public-domain witness rather than a falsely labelled freshly collated Greek critical edition.
translation.confidence: High for preservation of the historical witness's content; medium-high for the underlying Greek sense, subject to normal textual variants
translation.notes: All eighteen psalms are retained. Messianic language in Psalms 17–18 is not harmonized to later Christian terminology.
translation.license_note: The ancient text and the 1926 public-domain historical English witness are public domain. Hobah modernization is newly prepared for this project.
